name: RED1-1-the-authority-dropped
old: if (!Array.isArray(a.glyphs) || !a.glyphs.includes('dev')) return;   // silently: a stranger probing this learns nothing from being ignored
note: THE WHOLE SLICE. Any player in the room can then speak as the server, and a line that looks official is the most valuable forgery in the game: "the relay is restarting", "there is a duplication bug, log out now", "the developers are giving away X" - each costs a player something and each is free to whoever can make a line look official.

name: RED1-2-the-authority-read-off-the-frame
old: if (!Array.isArray(a.glyphs) || !a.glyphs.includes('dev')) return;   // silently: a stranger probing this learns nothing from being ignored
note: The same hole wearing a check. `a.glyphs` was written by `_named` off the VERIFIED claims and can be written by nothing else on that socket; `m.glyphs` is whatever the sender typed. ACC1g shut exactly this on the name one arc ago, and a title was already the stronger claim - the server's own voice is stronger still.

name: RED1-3-the-title-mistaken-for-the-grant
old: if (!Array.isArray(a.glyphs) || !a.glyphs.includes('dev')) return;   // silently: a stranger probing this learns nothing from being ignored
note: The WORN title is a choice - a developer who equips Founder instead would lose the ability to broadcast, and the grant would depend on a cosmetic preference. The dev GLYPH is the derived fact (server-account/src/titles.js: it rides the config list, not the column), which is why the authority hangs off it.

name: RED1-4-the-rate-gate-dropped
old: if (!this._spend(ws, now, redGate, 'rbucket', 'rdrops', 'too many lines')) return;
note: A compromised or careless developer account can then paint every screen in the game as fast as a socket will carry frames. The grant says WHO may speak; the bucket says how often, and a broadcast needs both - an authority with no rate is a single account away from an outage.

name: RED1-5-the-red-bucket-is-the-chat-bucket
note: Two different allowances sharing one bucket means each silently spends the other: a developer who has just talked cannot broadcast, and one who has just broadcast cannot talk. Separate spends, separate buckets - which is also why CHAT1 gave chat its own rather than borrowing the pose one.

name: RED1-6-a-rate-the-gate-cannot-express
note: THE FIRST CUT OF THIS SLICE, and the pins caught it. `tokenGate` starts a fresh bucket with `rate` tokens and a pass costs a whole one, so any rate below 1 refuses the FIRST frame and every frame after it - the feature reads as 'slow' in the source and is DEAD in the game. The constraint is now written at tokenGate's own door.

name: RED1-7-the-server-line-carries-a-name
old: const said = JSON.stringify({ t: 'red', text: m.text, at: now });
new: const said = JSON.stringify({ t: 'red', id: a.id, name: a.name, text: m.text, at: now });
note: Nobody is speaking a server line, and giving it a speaker is how it stops being one: a reader now has an id to attribute it to, a name to colour, and a person to blame - and the announcement becomes a player's line drawn in red, which is the thing net/chat.js's `system` note warns about from the other direction.

name: RED1-8-the-broadcast-becomes-a-chat-frame
old: const said = JSON.stringify({ t: 'red', text: m.text, at: now });
new: const said = JSON.stringify({ t: 'chat', text: m.text, red: true, at: now });
note: Then 'is this the server?' is a FIELD on a frame every player can send, and the client has to trust it. Its own frame type is the whole defence: a player cannot send `t:'red'` at all, so the client marks the line from the type and there is nothing on it to forge.

name: RED1-9-the-parser-lets-an-unbounded-line-through
old:
const text = typeof m.text === 'string' ? sanitizeChat(m.text) : '';
    return text ? { t: 'say', text } : { error: 'bad say' };
new: return typeof m.text === 'string' ? { t: 'say', text: m.text } : { error: 'bad say' };
note: A broadcast is not a licence to put four kilobytes of control characters over every screen in the game. It is a chat line and it is bounded like one, at both ends.

name: RED1-10-the-client-decides-who-may-broadcast
note: A second copy of an authority this side does not hold. It is wrong the moment a grant lapses or arrives, it invites the next reader to trust it, and it protects nothing - the relay is the only thing that can check a signature, and it already does.

name: RED1-11-the-red-line-is-not-a-system-line
note: Nobody is speaking a red line, so every reader that already knows what a system line is has to be told about this one separately - starting with ui/nameLayer.js's `bubbleLineOk`, which would hang a chat bubble over the head of a peer whose id is the empty string.

name: RED1-12-the-inbound-gate-dropped
old:
if (!this._lineIn(room, null, now)) return;
      this._deliver('chat', () => this.onRed?.({ text, at: Number.isFinite(m.at) ? m.at : now }));
new: this._deliver('chat', () => this.onRed?.({ text, at: Number.isFinite(m.at) ? m.at : now }));
note: CHAT-G's whole finding, on the one line type a dishonest relay would most want to flood. The relay a client talks to is the PLAYER'S OWN CHOICE (`?server=`, the Relay field), so 'the relay already gated this' is a sentence about an honest relay only - and net/chat.js keeps CHAT_KEEP lines, so an ungated stream is a player's history deleted.
